 Before
 Honourable Mr. Justice Kaushik Goswami
 Order
Date : 10.05.2024 Heard Mr. J. C. Gaur, learned counsel for the petitioners.

Also heard Mr. A. U.
Choudhury, learned counsel for the respondent Nos. 4, 5 and 6 in WP(C)/4972/2022 and Ms. B.
Choudhury for respondent No. 4 in WP(C)/4793/2022 along with Ms. S. Baruah, learned Govt.
Advocate for State respondents and Ms. G. Hazarika for respondent No. 1.

In the present two petitions, the petitioner is assailing non-payment of compensation to the petitioners/owners of the subject land, which was acquired under Section 6 (1) of the Assam Land (Requisition & Acquisition) Act, 1964.
Page No.# 6/7 The case of the petitioners is that they are permanent residents of village- Pub Majirgaon, P.S. Azara, P.O. Bhattapara Guwahati as Riyats/ tenants since long time.

It is the further case of the petitioners that petitioners and their predecessors-in-interest have been occupying and cultivating the aforesaid subject land since long time and in the year 2020-21, the Govt. had acquired their land along with other adjoining land for extension of airport without paying compensation to the petitioner.

It is submitted that representation has been filed before the District Commisioner, Kamrup as regards the payment of compensation against the subject land of the petitioners which is still not being attended to.
It further appears that there is some dispute as regards the entitlement of the compensation against the subject land between the land owners.

Today when the matter was called, there has been a consensus amongst the parties that this writ petition can be disposed of with a direction to the District Commisioner to dispose of the representation filed by the petitioners after hearing all the concerned parties within a reasonable period of time.

In view of the aforesaid concession made by the parties, this court disposes of the writ petitions with a direction to the District Commissioner to dispose of the representations dated 18.01.2024 filed by the petitioners, after hearing all the parties including the private respondents, within a period of 3(three) months of the date of receipt of certified copy of the order.
Page No.# 7/7 With the aforesaid observation and direction, this writ petition stands disposed of.
